subject: Exception request: first-token tradeoff vs sustained tokens for Greenline POC
messages:
From: Tom Benders <tbenders@greenline.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@greenline.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Greenline POC - streaming SLA clarifications

Hi Rachel / Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. A couple of technical asks from our infra team that will determine whether we push forward with the pilot next week:

- We need firm guidance on the acceptable tradeoff between Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and sustained token throughput for streaming endpoints. Greenline's UI needs first token under 400ms for interactive flows, but our batch scoring pipelines want sustained ~250 tokens/sec for larger transcripts.
- If Redwood can tolerate slightly higher TTFT (up to ~700ms) in exchange for guaranteed sustained throughput during burst windows, we can relax client-side buffering.

Can you propose an exception pathway or a carve-out that lets us run a mixed workload during the POC? If you need metrics, I attached a small sample of our expected request shape.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is aligning dates.

Thanks,
Tom

Attachments: greenline_poc_metrics.csv (CSV, 12KB)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Tom Benders <tbenders@greenline.com>, Priya Shah <pshah@greenline.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Greenline POC - streaming SLA clarifications

Tom / Priya —

Appreciate the clarity and the sample. Short answer: we can propose a scoped exception for the POC that relaxes the 1st-token SLO slightly while providing a separate guaranteed sustained token rate for the mixed workload windows. I want to align on exact thresholds and the rollback/fallback behavior.

Next steps I propose:
- Aditya and I will draft a proposed SLA matrix with two profiles: "interactive-priority" (strict TTFT) and "sustained-throughput" (guaranteed tokens/sec), including acceptable TTFT windows, token/sec targets, and regional failover behavior.
- We'll include guardrails: max burst duration, automatic downgrade to non-streaming endpoints if headroom is exceeded, and clear monitoring dashboards for you.
- Marissa, can you include estimated uplift to committed capacity and any commercial notes?

I'll aim to send a draft by EOD.

—Rachel

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Greenline POC - streaming SLA clarifications

Rachel / Marissa / Tom —

Draft proposal below (high level) — attaching a small SLA matrix workbook (redwood_sla_matrix_v1.xlsx) with numbers and the monitoring plan.

Proposal summary:
- POC scoped exception (30 days) with two concurrent routing profiles:
  * interactive-priority: TTFT <= 400ms target (p50), sustained token/sec best-effort, burst throttling enabled after 5s
  * throughput-priority: sustained >= 250 tokens/sec (regional aggregate), TTFT allowed up to 700ms (p95)
- Failure / fallback behavior:
  * If sustained rate falls below 85% of target for more than 60s, requests will be automatically rerouted to a non-streaming synchronous endpoint (same model family) to preserve throughput; clients receive an informational header and a short advisory in-stream.
- Monitoring & acceptance criteria:
  * We will publish a per-route dashboard with TTFT p50/p95 and sustained tokens/sec (1m/5m windows).
  * Greenline to provide a 24h representative trace set (we have sample CSV) and a set of acceptance prompts.
- Commercial/operational impacts:
  * Scoped uplift to reserved pool during POC: estimated 2x nominal capacity for 6 hours/day of peak testing. Marissa, see the workbook for a cost delta.

Caveats: this is a POC-level exception only. For production we recommend selecting the consistent profile that matches your primary UX.

Tom — tagging Priya on the monitoring expectations and Marissa on capacity. If this aligns, I'll prepare a short amendment and a runbook for the failover path.

Attachments: redwood_sla_matrix_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB)

—Aditya
Senior Product Engineer, Serving Runtime

Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Greenline POC - streaming SLA clarifications

Tom / Priya —

Thanks — this aligns with what we discussed. Confirming the POC exception as follows:

- Duration: 30 days starting once Greenline enables traffic to the POC endpoints.
- Profiles: interactive-priority (TTFT target: p50 <= 400ms) and throughput-priority (sustained >= 250 tokens/sec, p95 TTFT <= 700ms).
- Failover: automatic reroute to synchronous endpoint if sustained drops below 85% for >60s.
- Monitoring: per-route TTFT and tokens/sec dashboards; we will share a read-only dashboard link and a daily summary during high-test days.
- Commercial: scoped capacity uplift during test windows as shown in the attached workbook; Marissa will follow up on contract amendment and any temporary credits.

Action items:
- Greenline: confirm start date and provide a 24h trace set (Tom).
- Redwood: Aditya to publish the runbook and the amended SLA doc; Marissa to draft amendment (2 business days).

If Greenline confirms today we can kick off a staged ramp Wednesday.

Best,
Rachel
